title: Why Africa must enter the green industrialization race now
body:
The global green transition is not waiting for Africa.

- As green value chains rapidly consolidate around established processing hubs—especially in China—the window for late entry is narrowing fast. Countries that build processing capacity, set technological standards, and anchor supplier networks today will dominate green industries tomorrow.
- For Africa, delay carries a real risk: being locked into a long-term role as a supplier of raw or semi-processed minerals, while value, jobs, and technological capabilities are captured elsewhere. Once infrastructure, standards, and industrial ecosystems are entrenched outside the continent, catching up becomes exponentially harder.
- This is not about abundance of resources—Africa has those. It is about speed, coordination, and capability.

Entering the green industrialization race means:

- Moving beyond extraction to processing and manufacturing
- Designing regional green industrial strategies, not isolated national bets
- Aligning energy systems, industrial policy, and finance
- Using minerals as leverage for technology transfer and capability building

The green transition will define the next phase of global industrial leadership. Those who hesitate will supply it; those who act will shape it. Borrowing one of Mark Carney's line at Davos: "If you are not at the table, you are on the menu.”

⏱ Africa still has a choice—but not unlimited time.

Our recent report (https://lnkd.in/eJUPe8hF), relying on a regional developmentalism thinking, surfaces and interrogates key parameters that should inform a regionally coordinated strategy that assures green Industrial development victory for Africa by Africa.

Elvis K. Avenyo (Ph.D.) Solomon Owusu Woubet Kassa, PhD
